local:depends-ban-is-now-a-choice-not-a-.title:
`hk.pkl` bans `depends` in favour of `exclusive = true` because a failed
dependency used to deadlock every dependent (`hk.pkl:152`, and the same doctrine
in `long-running-command-hangs.md` rule 5 + dotfiles' `no_hk_depends` step). The
trigger condition is `fail_fast = false` AND a step carrying `depends`. This
repo sets the first at `hk.pkl:12` and, because of this very ban, has ZERO of the
second — the only occurrence of `depends` in `hk.pkl` is the comment forbidding
it. So the deadlock could never have fired here; the ban is what made it
unreachable, which is the point rather than a caveat to it.

**Upstream FIXED it in v1.53.0 (#1099): dependents no longer hang after a failed
dependency.** So the ban is no longer a workaround for a live defect — it is a
choice, and `tool-currency-and-native-first.md` says custom avoidance kept alive
by a fixed defect is exactly what to re-examine.

Deliberately NOT retired (Ray, 2026-07-31): `exclusive` works, the doctrine spans
both repos, and dotfiles machine-enforces it — retiring it here alone would split
the two repos' rules. Recorded WITH its version condition so a future reader knows
which of the two it is, and so any revival is a decision rather than a rediscovery.

local:hk-version-is-written-three-times.title:
dotfiles' `hk_version_parity` step does not port — it exists because
that repo carries THREE pkl files whose hk pins can drift apart, and this repo has
exactly ONE (`hk.pkl`, verified 2026-07-31).

But a drift surface remains on a DIFFERENT axis: the version appears three times
across two files — `mise.toml`'s `hk` pin, and `hk.pkl`'s `amends` and `import`
URLs. A `mise.toml`-only bump runs a new BINARY against the old SCHEMAS. Bump all
three together, or the mismatch shows up as a pkl error with nothing pointing at
the pin.
